motion-diagram.def: A picture of an object's position at equal time intervals, as dots or images, often with velocity arrows. Growing gaps mean speeding up; shrinking gaps, slowing down.

position-time-graph.def: A graph of position x against time t. Its slope at any instant is the velocity; a straight line means constant velocity, a curve means the velocity changes.

velocity-time-graph.def: A graph of velocity v against time t. Its slope is the acceleration and the area between it and the time axis is the displacement.

acceleration-time-graph.def: A graph of acceleration a against time t. The area between it and the time axis is the change in velocity.

constant-acceleration.def: Motion in which the velocity changes by the same amount in every equal time interval: a straight, sloped v-t graph and a horizontal a-t graph.

kinematic-equations.def: The three equations for constant acceleration: v = v₀ + at; x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at²; v² = v₀² + 2a(x − x₀). Each leaves out one quantity.

free-fall.def: Motion under gravity alone, with air resistance negligible. Near Earth every freely falling object has a constant acceleration g = 9.8 m/s² (about 10 m/s²) downward.

nonuniform-acceleration.def: Acceleration that changes with time: a curved v-t graph. In this course it is described from graphs and in words, not calculated.
